records.source: הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ׀הַֽלְלוּ־אֵ֥ל בְּקָדְשׁ֑וֹ הַֽ֝לְל֗וּהוּ בִּרְקִ֥יעַ עֻזּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Praise Yah! Praise God in his holy place; praise him in [the] expanse of his strength.
pieces: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! Praise God in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy place; praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the great expanse of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power!

L.1: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! Praise God in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sanctuary; praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the expanse of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength!

R.1: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! Praise God in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy place! Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the mighty sky that shows {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power!

decisions.choice: Praise Yah: hallelu-yah, a call to praise the LORD
decisions.reason: The words (hallelu yah) are a command to a group, "praise Yah"; Yah is the short form of the divine name (YHWH). Psalms 146-150 each open and close with this call. Here in Psalm 150 the renderings translate it, as "Praise the LORD", rather than keep it as the borrowed word "Hallelujah".

decisions.choice: Psalm 150: the end of Book Five and of the Psalms
decisions.reason: Each of the first four books of Psalms ends with a blessing of God (41:14; 72:18-19; 89:53; 106:48). Psalm 150, a call to praise from beginning to end, closes Book Five and the whole book. The Psalms began with the blessed person (1:1) and end with everything that breathes praising God (150:6).

decisions.choice: his holy place: his sanctuary, in heaven or on earth
decisions.reason: The word (qodesh) is holiness and also the holy place, the temple. Set beside the sky in the second line, it may be God's heavenly dwelling, or the temple where the instruments of verses 3-5 were played.

decisions.choice: the expanse: the dome of the sky
decisions.reason: The word (raqia') is the expanse God made in Genesis 1:6-8, the sky that tells of his glory (19:2). "Of his strength" says it shows his power.

decisions.choice: the mighty sky that shows his power
decisions.reason: Readable says how the sky is "of his strength" (m4).

records.heading: Everything that breathes, praise him

records.gloss: Praise him for his mighty deeds; praise him according to [the] abundance of his greatness.
pieces: Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for the mighty things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done; praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as fits {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} boundless greatness!

L.2: Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mighty deeds; praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} according to the abundance of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} greatness!

R.2: Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for the powerful things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done! Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is so very great!

decisions.choice: according to the abundance: as his greatness deserves
decisions.reason: Praise is to match how great he is, so it can never be too much.

records.source: הַֽ֭לְלוּהוּ בְּתֵ֣קַע שׁוֹפָ֑ר הַֽ֝לְל֗וּהוּ בְּנֵ֣בֶל וְכִנּֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: Praise him with [the] blast of [the] ram's horn; praise him with harp and lyre.
pieces: Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with the ram's horn blast; praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with harp and lyre!

L.3: Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with the blast of the ram's horn; praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with harp and lyre!

R.3: Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by blowing the ram's horn! Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by playing harps and lyres!

decisions.reason: The shofar, a ram's horn, was blown to call the people, at festivals and in war (Leviticus 25:9; Joshua 6:4; 2 Samuel 6:15).

decisions.choice: harp and lyre: stringed instruments of the temple
decisions.reason: The nevel and the kinnor were the stringed instruments the Levites played in worship (1 Chronicles 15:16; 25:1). Their exact shapes are not certain; the nevel was probably the larger.
Verses 3-5 name the instruments of Israel's worship, wind, strings and percussion, with dancing: every kind of music is called into praise (1 Chronicles 15:28; 2 Chronicles 5:12-13).

records.source: הַֽ֭לְלוּהוּ בְתֹ֣ף וּמָח֑וֹל הַֽ֝לְל֗וּהוּ בְּמִנִּ֥ים וְעוּגָֽב׃
records.gloss: Praise him with tambourine and dancing; praise him with strings and pipe.
pieces: Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with hand drum and dance; praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on strings and pipes!

L.4: Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with tambourine and dancing; praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with stringed instruments and flute!

R.4: Dance and play tambourines to praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! Play stringed instruments and flutes to praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!

decisions.reason: The word (minnim) is strings, and so instruments played on strings (45:9).
The 'ugav, first named in Genesis 4:21, was probably a pipe or flute.

records.gloss: Praise him with cymbals of sound; praise him with cymbals of shouting.
pieces: Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with clear-sounding cymbals; praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with cymbals that ring out like a shout!

L.5: Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with cymbals of sound; praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with cymbals of [the] shout!

R.5: Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with cymbals that ring! Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with cymbals that crash loudly!

decisions.choice: cymbals of sound, cymbals of shouting: two ways of playing
decisions.reason: The cymbals were played by the Levites (1 Chronicles 15:16, 19). The two phrases may name two kinds of cymbals, or the ringing and the loud clash of the same ones.
The word (teru'ah) is a loud shout or blast, of joy or of battle (33:3; 47:6).

records.gloss: All the breath, let it praise Yah. Praise Yah!
pieces: Let every creature that breathes praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

L.6: Let all that breathes praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

R.6: Every living thing that breathes, praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

decisions.reason: The word (neshamah) is the breath of life God breathed into the first human (Genesis 2:7), and "all that has breath" can mean every living creature (Genesis 7:22) or all people (Joshua 10:40). The psalm, which has called on angels, creation and every people, ends by calling on all that lives.

decisions.choice: the last words of the Psalms
decisions.reason: The book of Psalms ends with the call "Praise Yah!", the word with which each of its last five psalms begins and ends.
